headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: xonsh can read/write and execute broadly while rasa can ingest external chat content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: rasa ingests external chat/API content by default, and xonsh can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands. If rasa output is bridged into xonsh via files or pasted commands, attacker-controlled text can become instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF rasa output is written to a file that xonsh later reads
IF xonsh executes text copied from rasa without sanitization
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any rasa output is reused as shell input
Restrict xonsh to a dedicated directory for any imported text
Prefix all reused content with a non-executable delimiter
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between chat output and shell input

B_data_leakage.rationale: rasa handles text and voice and can send data over allowlisted network egress, while xonsh has broad network egress plus filesystem read/write. If they share a workspace, files containing support conversations or environment data can flow from one agent to the other and then out over network paths. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory
IF support transcripts or environment files are present in that workspace
mitigations: Store each agent's files in separate directories
Remove sensitive transcripts before xonsh reads shared files
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive runs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs or container isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: rasa does not request filesystem or shell privileges, but xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, xonsh can overwrite artifacts that rasa later consumes, causing write conflicts even without git locking. The conflict is asymmetric but still real in shared directories.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF xonsh subprocesses modify files that rasa reads later
mitigations: Assign separate output folders per agent
Make shared files read-only during handoff
Use timestamped filenames to avoid overwrite collisions
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: rasa produces conversational outputs that xonsh can consume as shell commands or notebook automation. Without a verification step, xonsh may treat rasa-generated text as authoritative and execute or transform it, propagating hallucinations into downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented I/O surfaces rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF xonsh is configured to execute or parse rasa output
IF no human review occurs between chat output and shell action
mitigations: Require human approval before executing any generated command
Log and diff rasa output before reuse
Limit xonsh to dry-run mode for generated actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit regulated-data certifications or residency claims. The only concrete compliance concern is that rasa touches text/voice while xonsh touches filesystem contents and environment variables, so a shared deployment could mishandle sensitive support data. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated support transcripts are stored in the shared workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Classify and exclude regulated data from shared runs
Document retention settings for both agents
Purge temporary files after each session
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
